question: Why do I feel distant from Allah?
short_answer: The Quran describes closeness as immediate and without condition. The feeling of distance is a feeling, not a fact. The Quran speaks to it directly.

sections.heading: The Quran names nearness
sections.body: The Quran does not describe Allah as distant. It describes Him as near, closer than the self.

evidence.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
evidence.translation_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.
evidence.why_cited: The answer is placed directly after the question.

evidence.arabic: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ
evidence.translation_en: And We are closer to him than his jugular vein.
And He is with you wherever you are.

sections.heading: The feeling of distance
sections.body: The Quran describes a heart that has drifted, not a Lord who has left. The distance is from the side of the one who feels it.

evidence.arabic: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ
evidence.translation_en: Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah?
evidence.why_cited: It names the slow hardening of the heart over time.

evidence.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ
evidence.translation_en: Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.
evidence.why_cited: It names the inner change as the starting point.
It names disease as a state that can settle in the heart.

sections.heading: What brings the heart back
sections.body: The Quran names remembrance, forgiveness, and return as the way back. The door is held open.

evidence.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ
evidence.translation_en: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah.'
evidence.why_cited: The address is to those who went too far, not the perfect.

evidence.translation_en: And return to your Lord and submit to Him.
evidence.why_cited: The call to return is placed right after the mercy.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا
evidence.translation_en: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
evidence.why_cited: The promise is tied to seeking forgiveness.

sections.heading: The nearness that does not change
sections.body: The Quran places nearness as a constant. It is not dependent on how the heart feels in the moment.

evidence.arabic: قُلْ إِن ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِي ۖ وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي ۚ إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ
evidence.translation_en: Say, 'If I err, I err only to my own loss, and if I am rightly guided, it is because of what my Lord has revealed to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and Near.'
evidence.why_cited: It joins hearing and nearness together.

evidence.translation_en: Indeed, my Lord is Near and Responsive.

evidence.arabic: فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۚ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
evidence.translation_en: Indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.
evidence.why_cited: It names both nearness and response in one verse.
